Interview cheatsheet

A revision plan for the last two hours, then every topic across the prep tracks in one line each, linked to the full answer. Tick "Must-know only" for a 30-minute pass.

Last 2 hours: revision plan

Want full recaps instead of one-liners? Use the 2-Hour Review in interview-prep: 13 timed blocks. Otherwise work top to bottom here. Tick steps as you go (saved in this browser). Short on time? Start at 60 minutes and use "Must-know only".

Timeline

Say-it-straight guardrails

  • Use "I built / I worked on" only for what you did. "I did not own that, here is how I would find out" is a strong answer.
  • No invented numbers. If you cannot reproduce a figure, retract it and give the underlying facts.
  • Never claim experience or platform ownership you do not have.
  • For any design question: clarify, estimate, boundaries, data, failure modes, trade-offs. Say what you would measure.
  • Stuck? Restate the question, state assumptions, answer the part you know, flag the rest.

Verify before you walk in

  • The actual framework and library versions you will talk about.
  • Which specific mechanisms you really used (queues, caching, tracing) versus which you would add.
  • One real performance or quality win with a before and after number, or plan to say you have none.
  • One mentoring or leadership example with a named outcome.
Numbers to know cold: ALB idle timeout 60 s. Heroku idle 55 s, SIGTERM grace 30 s. RAM ~100 ns, Redis ~1 ms, same-region network 1 to 2 ms, cross-continent ~100 to 150 ms.
